extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent agents filing in India (including applicants using PCT/Convention routes)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal rules for drafting and structuring patent claims, and for related filing topics (priority, divisional applications, patents of addition, convention/PCT filings) under Indian law and PCT practice. Covers claim clarity, format, priority dates, divisional and PCT procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance claim scope (not too broad or too narrow)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Claim must not be too broad to embrace more than what the applicant has in fact invented (may encroach on public domain or others' subject matter). A claim must not be too narrow because such a Claim would not be sufficiently effective against potential infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Claim which is too broad may encroach upon the subject matter which is in public domain or belongs to others. If claims were too narrow an infringer would go scot-free and the full benefit of the invention may not accrue to the inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple claims to cover different scopes/aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Having many claims, where each claim has a different scope, allows the applicant to have a legal title to different aspects of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good drafting may begin with broad claims and develop towards claims that are narrower in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid terms that confuse scope or are non‑specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms of the claim which confuse the scope of the invention, or claims that are not specific (e.g. 'Any novel matter') should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid words that cause subjective judgment (e.g. 'thin', 'strong', 'a major part', 'such as', 'when required', 'any') unless such expression follows some definite value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be for a product or process and be one sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim shall be for the protection of either a product or process, as the case may be, and shall be in one sentence according to the standard practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim should be in a single sentence and should be clearly worded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims formatting and preamble requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of invention in the complete specification is to be followed by a 'statement of Claims' preceded by the prescribed preamble, 'I / We claim' as the case may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should start from a fresh page, after detailed description of the invention and should be serially numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims should not be verbose
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim should not be verbose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise; clarity is preferred and verbosity to be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: No restriction on number of claims (fees apply after ten)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no restriction as to the number of claims that can be incorporated in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has to pay additional fee, if total number of claims are more than ten.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be fairly based on matter disclosed in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim should be fairly based on matter disclosed in the specification. All the characteristics of the invention that form part of the Claims must be fully explained in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim should be complete so that it covers the inventive feature and enough elements around it to put the invention in the proper context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms in claims must appear in or be clearly inferred from description
rubrics_metrics.description: Any term which is used in the claim must be either found in the description or clearly inferred from the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade marks generally not to be used in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade Marks are an indication of the origin rather than the composition or content of goods, and should not be used in Patent Applications where a generic term can be used instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade Marks are only permitted in Claims where it can be shown that their use is unavoidable and does not introduce ambiguity. Where registered marks are mentioned, they should be acknowledged as such. If a Trade Mark is not registered, its owner should be indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim parts: preamble, transitional phrase, body
rubrics_metrics.description: A Claim usually consists of three parts: preamble, transitional phrase; and body. The introductory phrase identifies the category of the invention and sometimes the purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional phrases may be words/phrases such as 'comprising', 'including', 'consisting of', 'consisting essentially of'. If an invention is an improvement on prior art, characterize the claim with 'characterized by' or 'wherein' to distinguish prior art (prior art before 'characterized by', inventive features after). Example provided for a 'data input device comprising...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent (principal) claim requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The first claim is always an independent claim (Principal Claim). It should clearly define the essential novel features of the most preferred embodiment of the process/product that constitutes the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claim may be properly characterized with respect to the prior art, defining all the technical features essential to the invention or inventive concept. The claim should bring out sufficient details of interrelationship, operation or utility to establish that the invention achieves the intended objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit number and ensure cognate character of independent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be more than one independent claim if claims fall under a single inventive concept, but it is advisable to limit the number of claims and independent claims so that the claims are all of cognate character and linked to form a single inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of multiple independent claims directed at non-cognate aspects is not desirable. If claims relate to a plurality of distinct inventions it may be objected on the ground of lack of unity of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims: antecedence and permissible content
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim derives antecedence from an independent claim and reads into it the features of the independent claim and may contain additional non-essential features and optional features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims may include minute aspects and optional features (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims must be fully limited by preceding independent claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent Claims that are not fully limited by the terms of the preceding independent claim (e.g. dependent claims which omit, modify or substitute a feature of an independent claim) are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsearchable claims (excessive alternatives or parameter choices)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim which is unsearchable by reason of the number of alternatives embraced, or the choice of characterizing parameters should not be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omnibus claim is not allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of including an omnibus claim does not have any legal basis under the Patent Act and such a claim cannot be allowed (Section 10(4)(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omnibus claims are unclear, vague and unsearchable and are desirable to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each claim must have a priority date
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim of a complete specification shall have a priority date. If the complete specification is filed along with the application, the date of filing of the application is the date of the priority of the claim(s) of the specification if the claim(s) are fairly based on the matter disclosed in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rule establishing that priority attaches at the claim level; dependent on fair basis in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority when complete specification filed pursuant to provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Complete Specification is filed pursuant to a Provisional Specification, the priority date thereof shall be the date of filing of the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority for complete specification based on multiple cognate provisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complete specification is filed based on two or more provisional specifications which are cognate, the priority dates for claims arising from each of the provisional specifications will be the date of the respective provisional specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority on conversion between complete and provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complete specification is converted into a provisional specification and a fresh complete specification is filed thereafter, the priority date of claims shall be the date of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11(3) addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller may cancel provisional and postdate it to complete filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complete specification is filed after the provisional specification, the Controller may on the request of the applicant made any time before the grant, cancel the provisional specification and postdate the provisional specification to the date of complete specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority when claim is based partly on different previous applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Claim is fairly based on the matter disclosed partly in one and partly in another such previous application accompanying provisional specification, the priority date of the claim shall be the date of the later filed Specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority from earlier Indian application filed within 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete specification based on a previously filed application in India has been filed within twelve months from the date of that application and the claim is fairly based on the matter disclosed in the previously filed application, the priority date of that claim shall be the date of the previously filed application in which the matter was first disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against invalidation by publication/use or later patent (Section 11(3A))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim in a complete specification of a patent shall not be invalidated by reason only of: (a) the publication or use of the invention so far as claimed in that claim on or after the priority date of such claim; or (b) the grant of another patent which claims the invention, so far as claimed in the first mentioned claim, in a claim of the same or a later priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11(3A) provides protection in specified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application allowed when complete specification contains more than one invention
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complete specification contains more than one invention, the applicant may divide the application and file further application(s) in respect of inventions disclosed in the provisional or complete specification already filed; such division shall only be based on plurality of invention in the first mentioned specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination of a divisional application shall always be done in conjunction with the main application to avoid double patenting. Maintainability decided by the Controller after examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application filing date and patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of filing of a divisional application shall be the same as that of the main application, from which it has been divided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term of patent for a divisional application shall be twenty years from the date of filing of main application or international filing date in case the application was divided out of National phase application under PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application contents and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Divisional Application should be filed along with a Complete Specification. The Claims of the Divisional Application shall not conflict with those of main application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 16(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application priority and prohibition on further division
rubrics_metrics.description: The Divisional Application is treated as a substantive Application and is accorded the date of filing of the main Application. A divisional application shall be examined in conjunction with the first mentioned application so as to avoid claim overlap resulting in double patenting. A divisional application cannot be further divided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 16, Explanation; Section 11(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application jurisdiction and reference requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application shall be filed in the same jurisdiction as that of the main application and the Complete Specification accompanying the Divisional Application shall contain a specific reference to the main application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 4; R.13(2). Change of agent does not affect jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees applicable to divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For all purposes under the Patents Act, the Divisional Application is treated as a substantive application and, hence all fee applicable to a patent application shall be payable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent of Addition: when and filing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant comes up with an improvement or modification of the invention described or disclosed in main application, the applicant may make an application for Patent of Addition. An Application for a Patent of Addition shall be filed on the same or subsequent date of filing of the Application for main Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Patent of Addition shall be granted only after the grant of the main patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent of Addition: conversion, renewal, expiry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patentee holds two patents, it is possible to convert one of the independent patents to a patent of addition of the other, if the subject matter was an improvement or modification. There is no need to pay separate renewal fee for the Patent of Addition during the term of the main patent. A patent of addition expires along with the main patent. However, if the main patent is revoked, the patent of addition may be converted into an independent patent if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date of filing shall be the date on which the application for patent of addition has been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent of Addition: inventive step and novelty interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for Patent of Addition cannot be challenged on the ground of lack of inventive step with respect to the disclosure in the main application or patent. But the disclosure in main application or patent may be cited for novelty against the application for patent of addition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent of Addition: reference requirement in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete specification of application for patent of addition shall include specific reference to the number of main patent or the application for main patent, and a definite statement that the invention comprises an improvement in, or a modification of the invention claimed in the specification of the main patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 13(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention application: right of priority (Paris Convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person has made an Application in a Convention country (basic application), and makes an application in India within twelve months, the priority date of a claim of the complete specification based on matter disclosed in the basic application is the date of making of the basic application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several convention applications were filed, the twelve month period is reckoned from the earliest of those applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention application: required documents and formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Every convention application shall be accompanied by a complete specification; an abstract; specify the date on which and the convention country in which the basic application was made; and state that no application for protection had been made in a convention country before that date by the applicant or by any person from whom he derives title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certified copy of the priority document may be required within 3 months if requested; translations required if not in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention application: term and division
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of patent of a convention application shall be twenty years from the date of filing of the Application in India. A Convention Application can be divided, and the divided Application shall have the same priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Convention Application shall not be post-dated under subsection (1) of section 17 to a date later than the date on which under the provisions of this Act the application could have been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT filing options for Indian applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: An Indian applicant can file a PCT International application via: (a) Indian Patent Office as receiving office after taking permission under section 39; (b) filing directly at the International Bureau after permission under section 39; (c) after filing in India, within 12 months file an international at IB after taking permission under section 39 if within 6 weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international application required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Application should contain a request, a description, one or more claims, one or more drawings (where required) and an abstract. It should comply with the prescribed physical requirements, be in a prescribed language, and required fee should be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request may be computer printout; request should contain petition, title, applicant/inventor/agent details, declaration of inventorship signed appropriately, details of priority and indication of competent International Searching Authority, optional indications such as priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT language, abstract, claims and drawings standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Language of International Application must be one the Receiving Office accepts. Abstract is intended for technical information and cannot be used to interpret scope; should be 50–150 words summarizing technical problem, gist of solution and principal use. Claims must define subject matter and be clear, concise and fully supported by the description. Drawings required only when necessary for understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Application is filed in India it has to be in English or Hindi (Hindi must have verified English translation). The request must be in a language accepted by the Receiving Office and one of the publication languages. Sequence listings and electronic filing rules apply as per PCT provisions and Applicant’s Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office checks and international filing date conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Receiving Office accords the date of receipt as international filing date provided at time of receipt: (i) applicant has right to file with that Office; (ii) application is in prescribed language; (iii) application contains an indication it is intended as international application, designation of at least one contracting state, name of applicant, a part appearing to be a description, a part that appears to be claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If missing, Office invites correction; correction within time can preserve filing date. The Office also checks other defects (signature, applicant indications, title, abstract, physical requirements) and may invite correction within time limits or declare application withdrawn. Typical correctable defects listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal to IB and ISA and treatment of missing items
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office transmits a 'record copy' to the International Bureau and a 'search copy' to the International Searching Authority and keeps a 'home copy'. Transmittal does not take place while national security prescriptions apply. If drawings referred to are missing, applicant may furnish within two months or reference is considered non-existent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record copy mailed promptly and not later than five days before expiration of 13th month from priority date; search copy transmitted at time of transmittal except where search fees unpaid.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT fees and fee correction
rubrics_metrics.description: All PCT fees are subject to change. Transmittal fee given in First Schedule. Failure to pay or underpayment can be corrected under PCT rule 16bis; invitation to pay missing fees will be issued; payment within a month of international filing date or later with a late payment fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indian applicants generally remit international filing and search fees in US Dollars by demand draft to Controller of Patents at State Bank of India, New York Branch; transmittal fee payable in INR to Controller of Patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: International search and Article 19 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: International Search report is established by the International Searching Authority. Applicant may amend the Claims under Article 19 in light of the International Search Report with effect in all designated States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limit for Article 19 amendments: two months from transmittal of the international search report to IB and to applicant, or 16 months from priority date, whichever is later. Amendments received after time limit may be treated as received on last day if before technical preparations for publication are complete. Amendments can save costs for local filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of international application (PCT Rule 90bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw the international application at any time prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is effective on receipt of a notice addressed by the applicant to the International Bureau, to the receiving Office or, where Article 39(1) applies, to the International Preliminary Examining Authority.
